Olympic Park gets Quebec’s first solar-powered public space

September 16, 2026
By Construction Canada
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:19
Instaread

A new public space at Montreal’s Olympic Park demonstrates the integration of solar power into the built environment.

Urban design firm Aire commune has unveiled Espace solaire, billed as Quebec’s first outdoor public space powered entirely by solar energy.

The permanent installation combines public amenities, renewable energy generation, and energy storage. It is designed to support people who want to gather, relax, or work outdoors.

The project uses shaded structures, integrated furniture, Wi-Fi-enabled workspaces, electrical outlets, and landscaping to support a range of use cases.

Solar panels form a visible part of the installation rather than sitting out of sight. They help power the space while also shaping its visual identity.

“Espace solaire embodies our vision of creating meaningful, sustainable, and accessible public spaces,” said Philippe Pelletier, co-founder of Aire commune. “By fully integrating solar energy into the design, we are demonstrating that innovation, conviviality, and the energy transition can go hand in hand.”

Aire commune developed the project with Sunbird Énergie. “This project provides a tangible example of how on-site solar generation, energy storage, and intelligent power management can help support the province’s energy transition,” said Simon Lafleur, founder and president of Sunbird Énergie.

The project also supports Olympic Park’s broader transformation into a year-round urban park.
